payload.rationale: The supplied CDC report gives 3,471 confirmed U.S. cases through September 17. Exceeding 6,000 requires at least 2,530 additional cases over roughly 105 remaining days—about 169 per week, versus approximately 93 per week averaged over the year so far. Maintaining that year-to-date average would produce roughly 4,900 cases, below the threshold; this is a benchmark, not a transmission forecast. Reaching the threshold therefore requires substantial acceleration or reporting catch-up. The reported 39 new outbreaks and 95% outbreak-associated share indicate clustered transmission, making a large additional wave plausible, but they do not establish that incidence is currently accelerating. I assign a 25% chance, reflecting a below-threshold baseline with considerable outbreak uncertainty. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that outbreaks may already be declining or becoming contained, leaving the year-to-date average above the remaining-year rate. The strongest reason it could be too low is that recent transmission may already be far above that average; spread in susceptible communities, potentially amplified by school contacts, could generate enough cases to exceed 6,000. These are transfer assumptions, not observed trends in the supplied evidence. Settlement depends on the CDC count available under the expiration rules, not a later revised total.
limitations: No recent weekly incidence series, outbreak sizes, geographic distribution, or containment status is supplied.
The probability is a judgmental estimate, not the output of a fitted transmission or reporting model.
CDC counts are provisional; reporting delays, epidemiological-week assignment, and revisions before expiration can affect settlement. Revisions after expiration are excluded.
The supplied evidence packet is narrow and has not been independently verified.
